speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Thank you for sharing your symptoms. Given your fever, headache, and fatigue, have you experienced any visual disturbances like scotomas or shimmering lights recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old female at 30 weeks gestation. The patient presents with a sudden onset of fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. She reports the consumption of ice cream 3 days prior to the onset of symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any eye pain or changes in vision, such as blurred spots or flashing lights, which could indicate PRES or encephalitis? REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, and Viral Serology (CMV, West Nile). REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain without contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: WBC 15,000/μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, Platelets 200,000/μL; Comprehensive Metabolic Panel: AST Within normal limits, ALT Within normal limits, Bilirubin Within normal limits; Viral Serology: CMV and West Nile negative; MRI Brain: No evidence of PRES or encephalitis.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever. I also have Headache, Anorexia, Fatigue, Malaise.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Unremarkable. The patient is currently pregnant, at her 30th week of gestation. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol. No recent travels or contact with sick individuals. No known allergies.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies cough, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, diarrhea, or urinary symptoms. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES) secondary to viral infection in a pregnant patient.
